title: Iran Strikes UAE Oil Tankers in Strait of Hormuz; One Indian Sailor Killed, Several Injured
summary: Iranian missiles struck UAE-flagged oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, killing one Indian sailor and injuring six to eight others. India's Ministry of External Affairs summoned Iran's senior-most diplomat in New Delhi to protest the attack on Indian nationals aboard commercial vessels. The incident occurred amid an active US-Iran military conflict, with the US having launched multiple rounds of strikes on Iran. The attack on commercial shipping in a critical global waterway has sharply escalated geopolitical and economic tensions.
exam_angle: Tests knowledge of India's diplomatic protocol (summoning envoys), India's responsibility to protect its diaspora/sailors abroad, and the strategic importance of the Strait of Hormuz for India's energy security and trade.
key_facts: 1 Indian sailor killed, 6–8 injured in Iranian missile strikes on UAE tankers in Hormuz
MEA summoned Iran's senior-most diplomat; action taken by Ministry of External Affairs
Strait of Hormuz: ~20% of global oil trade passes through it; Iran and Oman share jurisdiction
Incident date: July 14, 2026

title: US Announces 20% Toll on Ships Using Strait of Hormuz; Trump Claims Control of Waterway
summary: US President Donald Trump announced a 20% fee (toll) on all cargo ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz, alongside a proposed blockade of Iran. Trump claimed the US would function as 'guardian' of the strait and should be reimbursed by nations benefiting from its security. Iran rejected the demand, calling it excessive. The move has significant implications for global oil trade, India's energy imports, and international maritime law under UNCLOS.
exam_angle: Relevant to international maritime law (UNCLOS — right of innocent passage through international straits), India's energy security (over 60% of India's crude oil imports transit Hormuz), and US-Iran geopolitics.
key_facts: Trump proposed 20% toll on all cargo transiting Strait of Hormuz
Strait of Hormuz: bordered by Iran and Oman; ~21 million barrels of oil/day pass through it
UNCLOS guarantees 'transit passage' rights through international straits
India imports ~60–65% of its crude oil from the Gulf; heavily exposed to Hormuz disruptions

title: UAE Plans New Port on East Coast to Bypass Strait of Hormuz
summary: The UAE announced plans to build a new port on its east coast (facing the Gulf of Oman) to reduce dependence on the Strait of Hormuz amid escalating US-Iran conflict. The port would allow UAE oil exports to bypass the strait entirely. State oil company ADNOC also tweaked offshore oil pricing to support non-Hormuz supply routes. This is a significant strategic infrastructure response to the crisis.
exam_angle: Relevant to understanding alternative maritime routes, energy security strategy, and the geopolitical significance of the Strait of Hormuz for Gulf nations and global trade.
key_facts: UAE planning new east coast port to bypass Strait of Hormuz
Port would face the Gulf of Oman, allowing direct access to Indian Ocean
UAE's ADNOC adjusting pricing to support alternate supply routes
Existing UAE bypass: Habshan–Fujairah pipeline (capacity ~1.5 mb/d)

title: India Launches UNSC Campaign for 2028–29 Term; Jaishankar Unveils 'SHANTI' Vision
summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar formally launched India's campaign for a non-permanent seat on the UN Security Council for the 2028–29 term, unveiling the 'SHANTI' vision as India's guiding framework. SHANTI stands for India's priorities at the UNSC — encompassing maritime security, seafarer safety, counter-terrorism financing, and a more inclusive global order. Jaishankar also met UN Secretary-General to discuss Middle East and Ukraine crises. India simultaneously pushed for a permanent UNSC seat as part of broader UN reform.
exam_angle: Directly relevant to India's foreign policy priorities, UNSC reform, India's bid for permanent membership, and current multilateral diplomacy. 'SHANTI' vision is a high-probability exam fact.
key_facts: India campaigning for UNSC non-permanent seat for 2028–29 term
EAM Jaishankar unveiled 'SHANTI' vision as India's UNSC agenda
SHANTI focuses on: maritime security, seafarer safety, terror financing crackdown
India is pushing for permanent UNSC membership as part of UN Security Council reform

title: NIA Court Issues Non-Bailable Warrant Against LeT Founder Hafiz Saeed in Pahalgam Terror Attack Case
summary: A National Investigation Agency (NIA) court issued a non-bailable warrant (NBW) against Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) founder Hafiz Saeed in connection with the Pahalgam terror attack. Saeed, already convicted in Pakistan on terror financing charges and designated a global terrorist by the UN, is now formally accused in the Pahalgam case. The NIA has jurisdiction over cross-border terrorism cases under the NIA Act, 2008. This marks a significant legal step linking Pakistan-based terror outfits to the attack.
exam_angle: Tests knowledge of NIA's jurisdiction, NBW provisions under CrPC/BNSS, India's counter-terrorism legal framework, and Pakistan-sponsored terrorism — all key polity/internal security themes.
key_facts: NIA court issued NBW against Hafiz Saeed for Pahalgam terror attack
Hafiz Saeed: founder of Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT); UN-designated global terrorist
NIA operates under NIA Act, 2008; has jurisdiction over terrorism cases
Pahalgam attack: occurred in Jammu & Kashmir; investigated by NIA
source: The Times of India / The Hindu

title: Supreme Court Questions Misuse of POCSO Act in Teen Relationships
summary: The Supreme Court of India raised concerns about the misuse of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, in cases involving consensual relationships between teenagers. The Court noted that POCSO, designed to protect children from sexual abuse, was being invoked in cases where both parties were minors engaged in consensual relationships, leading to the criminalisation of normal adolescent behaviour. The observation has implications for judicial interpretation and potential legislative review of the Act.
exam_angle: Relevant to GS Paper 2 (Polity/Governance) — POCSO Act provisions, judicial interpretation, child rights, and the balance between child protection and individual liberty. SC observations often precede policy changes.
key_facts: POCSO Act, 2012: protects children (under 18) from sexual offences
SC raised concern about POCSO being misused in consensual teen relationships
POCSO is a strict liability statute — consent is not a defence for accused
Issue touches on Articles 14, 19, 21 of the Constitution

title: India's Goods Trade Deficit Widens to 5-Month High Amid Hormuz Disruptions
summary: India's merchandise trade deficit hit a five-month high as imports surged, partly due to disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz driving up crude oil import costs. Weak exports also contributed to the widening deficit. India's imports from China soared to $80 billion in the first half of 2026, with exports to China up 37%. The US-Iran conflict is simultaneously raising inflation risks for India through elevated oil prices and potential El Niño impacts on food inflation.
exam_angle: Key for GS Paper 3 (Economy) — India's trade balance, current account deficit, crude oil import dependence, China trade asymmetry, and imported inflation are all standard exam themes.
key_facts: India's trade deficit at 5-month high; imports surged due to Hormuz-linked oil price rise
India's imports from China: $80 billion in H1 2026; India's exports to China up 37%
Inflation risks mounting: US-Iran tensions + El Niño = dual supply-side shock
India imports ~85% of its crude oil requirement
source: Reuters / The Times of India / Bloomberg

title: India–US Trade Deal: Framework Agreed; Competitive Advantage Clauses Still Under Discussion
summary: India and the United States agreed on a broad framework for a bilateral trade deal, but negotiations on 'competitive advantage' aspects — including tariff concessions and market access — remain ongoing. New Delhi stated it is holding out for better terms in areas such as agriculture, digital trade, and intellectual property. Reports indicate India is in a stronger negotiating position ('emboldened') given US interest in diversifying away from China. The deal framework was described as a significant step in India-US economic engagement.
exam_angle: India-US trade relations are a recurring GS Paper 2 (IR) and GS Paper 3 (Economy) topic — relevant to BTA, WTO commitments, and India's trade strategy.
key_facts: India-US trade deal framework agreed as of July 2026
Contentious issues: competitive advantage clauses, tariff concessions, digital trade
India is US's 9th largest trading partner; bilateral trade ~$190 billion
India holding out on agriculture market access and IPR provisions

title: Government Receives Revised Bids for IDBI Bank Stake Sale from Fairfax, Emirates NBD
summary: The Indian government received revised financial bids for its strategic disinvestment of IDBI Bank from two shortlisted bidders — Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings and UAE-based Emirates NBD. The government and Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) together hold over 94% stake in IDBI Bank and plan to sell a combined ~61% stake. The IDBI Bank privatisation is one of the flagship disinvestment initiatives under the government's asset monetisation and privatisation agenda.
exam_angle: IDBI Bank privatisation is a standard exam topic under GS Paper 3 (Economy) — disinvestment policy, banking sector reforms, and the role of LIC as a major shareholder.
key_facts: Revised bids received from Fairfax (Canada) and Emirates NBD (UAE) for IDBI Bank stake
Government + LIC hold ~94% in IDBI Bank; plan to sell ~61% stake
IDBI Bank privatisation: part of Union Budget disinvestment targets
IDBI Bank was categorised as 'private sector bank' by RBI after LIC acquired majority stake in 2019

title: Karnataka CM Announces India's First Government-Driven AI University
summary: Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah announced that Karnataka would establish India's first government-driven Artificial Intelligence (AI) university. The institution aims to position Karnataka — already home to Bengaluru, India's tech capital — as a leader in AI education, research, and innovation. The announcement aligns with India's National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence (NSAI) and the IndiaAI Mission launched by the Union government.
exam_angle: Relevant to GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech) — India's AI policy, IndiaAI Mission, skill development, and state-level tech governance initiatives.
key_facts: Karnataka to establish India's first government-driven AI university
Announced by CM Siddaramaiah
India's National Strategy for AI (NSAI) released by NITI Aayog in 2018
IndiaAI Mission: Union government initiative with Rs 10,372 crore outlay (2024)

title: Sonam Wangchuk on Day 16 of Hunger Strike at CJP Protest; Loses 8.2 kg
summary: Climate activist and engineer Sonam Wangchuk continued his hunger strike for the 16th consecutive day at an ongoing protest related to demands for constitutional protections for Ladakh. Wangchuk has lost 8.2 kg and demands the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal announced he would meet Wangchuk on July 16, 2026. The protest is linked to demands for Sixth Schedule protections and statehood for Ladakh.
exam_angle: Relevant to GS Paper 2 (Polity) — Sixth Schedule of the Constitution, Ladakh's status as a Union Territory without a legislature, tribal rights, and civil society activism.
key_facts: Sonam Wangchuk: Ladakh-based activist-engineer; hunger strike for 16 days as of July 14, 2026
Key demands: Sixth Schedule protection for Ladakh, full statehood for Ladakh
Ladakh became a Union Territory (without legislature) on October 31, 2019 under J&K Reorganisation Act
Sixth Schedule: provides autonomy to tribal areas in NE India; Ladakh seeks inclusion

title: Oil Prices Surge to One-Month High; Indian Markets Fall as US-Iran Conflict Escalates
summary: Crude oil prices surged to a one-month high as the US-Iran conflict escalated, with the Strait of Hormuz crisis disrupting global energy markets. India's Sensex fell over 553 points in early trade as rising oil prices dented market sentiment. Indian airlines, particularly newer carriers, began seeking emergency funding as aviation turbine fuel (ATF) costs surged. The dual risk of higher crude oil prices and weakening rupee poses a significant macroeconomic challenge for India.
exam_angle: Classic GS Paper 3 (Economy) theme — impact of crude oil price shocks on India's fiscal deficit, CAD, inflation, and currency. Also tests understanding of India's energy import dependence.
key_facts: Crude oil hit one-month high; Brent crude surged amid Hormuz crisis
Sensex fell 553 points on July 14, 2026 due to oil price spike
India's oil import bill ~$150 billion/year; every $10/barrel rise = ~$15 billion additional outgo
ATF comprises ~35–40% of airline operating costs in India
source: The Hindu / The Times of India / Moneycontrol

title: Vietnam Boat Tragedy: Bodies of 15 Indians Return to Mumbai
summary: The mortal remains of 15 Indians killed in a boat accident in Vietnam were repatriated and arrived in Mumbai. The victims, including at least one Andhra Pradesh resident for whom it was his maiden air travel, were among a group of Indian tourists caught in the tragedy. India's consular officials coordinated the repatriation. The incident highlights risks faced by Indian tourists abroad and the role of Indian diplomatic missions in consular assistance.
exam_angle: Relevant to India's consular services, diaspora protection, and the role of MEA's consular wing — important for GS Paper 2 (IR) and governance questions on Indian diaspora welfare.
key_facts: 15 Indians killed in Vietnam boat accident; bodies repatriated to Mumbai
At least one victim from Andhra Pradesh
Consular assistance provided by Indian diplomatic mission in Vietnam
MEA's consular wing oversees emergency assistance to Indians abroad
source: The Times of India / Deccan Herald

title: India's Imports from China Hit $80 Billion in H1 2026; Trade Asymmetry Grows
summary: India's imports from China soared to $80 billion in the first half of 2026, while India's exports to China rose 37% in the same period. Despite the export growth, the bilateral trade deficit with China remains structurally large. India continues to import significant volumes of electronics, solar panels, active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), and industrial machinery from China. The asymmetry is a persistent concern for India's manufacturing competitiveness and supply chain security.
exam_angle: India-China trade deficit is a standard GS Paper 3 (Economy) topic — linked to PLI schemes, Atmanirbhar Bharat, API dependence, and import substitution policy.
key_facts: India's imports from China: $80 billion in H1 2026
India's exports to China: up 37% in H1 2026
India-China trade deficit: one of India's largest bilateral deficits
Key imports from China: electronics, solar cells, APIs, machinery

title: IIT Bhubaneswar Researchers Develop Technology for Faster Computers
summary: Researchers at IIT Bhubaneswar have developed a new semiconductor technology aimed at building significantly faster computers. The innovation focuses on improving transistor performance, potentially overcoming limitations of traditional silicon-based chips. The development is significant in the context of India's push for semiconductor self-sufficiency under the India Semiconductor Mission and the Semicon India Programme.
exam_angle: Relevant to GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech) — semiconductor technology, India Semiconductor Mission, and India's push for self-reliance in critical technology.
key_facts: IIT Bhubaneswar developed new technology to build faster computers
Focus: improving semiconductor/transistor performance beyond silicon limitations
India Semiconductor Mission: Rs 76,000 crore incentive scheme for semiconductor manufacturing
Semicon India Programme: launched 2021 to develop domestic chip ecosystem

title: India Women's Cricket Team Wins Historic Test at Lord's
summary: The Indian women's cricket team achieved a landmark victory in a Test match at Lord's Cricket Ground, London — a historically significant result for women's cricket in India. Captain Harmanpreet Kaur reflected on the milestone win, describing it as an 'ode to pioneering women cricketers.' The victory is being hailed as a defining moment in the growth of women's cricket in India and comes as BCCI has been increasing investment in the women's game.
exam_angle: Relevant for GS Paper 1 (Society) or current affairs on women's empowerment in sports; Harmanpreet Kaur is a 'Person in News.' Lord's is a culturally significant venue (the 'Home of Cricket').
key_facts: India Women's cricket team won a Test match at Lord's, London
Captain: Harmanpreet Kaur
Lord's Cricket Ground: located in London; managed by Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC)
BCCI launched Women's IPL (WPL) in 2023 to boost women's cricket
